name: Transhumanist politics
summary: Transhumanist politics holds that science and technology should be used to overcome ageing, cognitive limits, suffering and confinement to Earth, with individuals free to choose enhancement. It is a family: libertarian, democratic (technoprogressive), anarcho- and left strands disagree over markets, regulation and distribution, but share pro-technology, pro-autonomy and cosmopolitan commitments and a concern for existential risk.
scope: The mainstream of the organised transhumanist movement as expressed in the Humanity+ Transhumanist Declaration, Bostrom's Transhumanist Values and the democratic/technoprogressive wing associated with James Hughes, which became the movement's centre after 2006. Libertarian and Extropian, anarcho- and left strands are noted where they diverge, and split issues are answered 0 or low. It is a philosophy-plus-movement rather than a party programme, so many economic answers are inferences.

keyFigures.name: James Hughes
keyFigures.role: Sociologist who coined democratic transhumanism and wrote Citizen Cyborg.

keyFigures.name: Nick Bostrom
keyFigures.role: Philosopher who co-founded the World Transhumanist Association and wrote on transhumanist values and existential risk.

keyFigures.name: Max More
keyFigures.role: Founder of Extropianism, whose politics moved from anarcho-capitalism toward liberal democracy.

sources.usedFor: Democratic regulation of technology, fair distribution, bodily autonomy

universal-healthcare.rationale: Democratic transhumanists propose including enhancement and anti-aging therapies in universal health care, though the libertarian wing opposes publicly insured enhancement.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Libertarian transhumanists say the free market best secures enhancement, while democratic and left strands want regulation and fair distribution, so adherents are genuinely split.

public-ownership.rationale: Only the left and anarcho strands favour collective ownership; the mainstream of the movement focuses on regulation and access rather than nationalising industries.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Hughes-style technoprogressives favour redistribution and equal access, while libertarians reject it; the movement as a whole is divided and never settled a tax position.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are not a transhumanist topic; democratic strands are union-friendly in general but libertarians and futurists are indifferent or hostile.

property-fundamental.rationale: Libertarian transhumanism rests on self-ownership and property, but democratic and left strands accept limits on property for fairness and safety.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Technoprogressives say technology is most empowering when regulated by legitimate democratic authorities, and Hughes called for limits on monopolies; libertarians dissent.

strong-leader.rationale: The Declaration calls for open forums and a social order for responsible decisions, and Bostrom proposes expanding democracy and rule of law; a leader bypassing checks conflicts with both.

state-harmful.rationale: Only the anarcho-transhumanist strand rejects the state; libertarian, democratic and left strands all assume some state or institutions.

traditional-family.rationale: Transhumanists favour reproductive freedom and see appeals to the natural as vague or an obstacle, so they do not treat traditional family structure as foundational.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Bostrom's values list diversity of sexual orientations and lifestyles, and the movement's liberal individualism supports legal equality.

more-religion-public.rationale: Transhumanism is secular in orientation and critiqued by religious thinkers, though some religious transhumanists exist; a larger public role for religion is not part of the program.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Declaration point 6 calls for solidarity across the globe and Bostrom lists species-wide values; the movement is cosmopolitan rather than nationalist.

gradual-change.rationale: Transhumanists seek radical transformation of the human condition and Bostrom argues for moving quickly, though the Declaration also urges responsible deliberation.

nation-first.rationale: Declaration point 6 calls for global solidarity, and Bostrom stresses international cooperation on existential risk, which cuts against national-interest first.

limit-growth.rationale: Bostrom treats productivity growth as a proxy for progress and the movement seeks to overcome natural limits; limiting growth contradicts the core aim.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Technogaianism and Viridian design tie some strands to green technology, but libertarians and others reject drastic government action; the movement has no unified line.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The Declaration opens by saying science and technology can overcome aging, cognitive limits, involuntary suffering and confinement to Earth, while warning of misuse; the faith in technological solutions is central.

experts-over-public.rationale: Transhumanists value research and foresight but democratic transhumanism insists on democratic governance; adherents are split between technocratic and democratic leanings.

central-planning.rationale: Bostrom warns that centrally planned efforts to create better people have a poor record, and libertarian and democratic strands alike reject planned economies.

basic-income.rationale: Hughes listed post-work and guaranteed minimum income as left-futurist trends for democratic transhumanism to incorporate, and automation makes it a common transhumanist theme, though libertarians dissent.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Left transhumanists link automation abundance to post-capitalist change, but most transhumanists do not seek to abolish money.

one-party-rule.rationale: Bostrom argues for expanding democracy and the rule of law, and every strand listed is democratic, libertarian or anarchist.

democracy-best.rationale: Bostrom proposes expanding democracy internationally and technoprogressives want technology governed by accountable democratic authorities, though libertarians and postpolitical strands doubt democracy.

natural-rulers.rationale: Bostrom and the Declaration affirm equal inclusion and wide access to enhancement, and reject the idea of a ruling elite by nature.

war-builds-character.rationale: Bostrom treats peace and cooperation as essential to avoiding catastrophe, so glorifying war contradicts transhumanist values.

separate-church-state.rationale: Transhumanism is secular in outlook and religious transhumanists exist but do not seek religious governance; secular government is the default.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religious critics oppose transhumanism and its policy rests on reason and autonomy rather than scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Only the anarcho-capitalist Extropian origins endorsed this, and More later moved away from it; the movement is split.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Bostrom's values include diversity of races and creeds, and the movement is universalist.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hughes seeks equal access to enhancement, which is equality of opportunity, while libertarians reject egalitarianism; not a stated aim of outcome equality.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: No transhumanist source discusses indigenous land rights, and the strands would not agree on it.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Libertarian transhumanism frames enhancement as a self-interested personal choice, but democratic strands stress solidarity, so the movement leans only mildly.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Declaration point 6 asks for policy that respects autonomy and individual rights, and the movement emphasises personal freedom.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Declaration point 7 extends well-being to all sentient beings, yet transhumanists see 'natural' as vague and technogaianism is a minority; no clear stance on intrinsic nature.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The movement is founded on optimism about technological civilisation, so calling it a disaster is opposed to its core.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Bostrom argues for moving quickly to give wide access to posthuman benefits, though also with caution on risks; the aim is rapid advancement.

human-enhancement.rationale: Declaration point 8 explicitly advocates wide personal choice over cognitive enhancement, life extension and reproductive technologies; Bostrom's morphological freedom says the same.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Postpolitical and singularitarian thinkers imagine reason-based post-democratic states, but mainstream strands stress democratic control of AI.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement aims to transform the human condition, and Declaration point 1 envisions overcoming present limits; restoration is the opposite orientation.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Bostrom's epistemic tentativeness and call for continual reassessment support a pragmatic stance, though the movement has its own ideological strands.

direct-action.rationale: The democratic and libertarian mainstream works through institutions, discussion and research; direct action is mostly an anarcho-transhumanist theme.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The Declaration frames technology as the means to overcome limits of aging and suffering, which a return to hunter-gatherer life would foreclose.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Left transhumanists want egalitarian access to abundance, but the movement as a whole does not endorse a need-based principle.

production-for-use.rationale: Only the left and anarcho strands criticise profit-driven production.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Only left transhumanists make this argument; libertarians reject it and democratic strands do not hold it.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The movement's democratic and rights-based commitments reject dictatorship, and Noonan argues Marxist transhumanism is incoherent in any case.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Left transhumanists critique capitalism but the claim of inevitable imperialism is not a movement position.

taxation-theft.rationale: Libertarian transhumanists hold it, while democratic transhumanists want taxes and public funding; the movement is genuinely split.

harm-principle.rationale: Declaration point 8 and Bostrom say moral objections alone are not grounds for coercion, which matches limiting state interference to preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Declaration point 6 stresses individual rights but also solidarity and well-being of all sentient beings including future minds, so rights are not confined to individuals as sole holders.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Libertarian and Extropian strands may favour exit, but democratic strands prioritise voice; split.

positive-liberty.rationale: Democratic transhumanists seek equal access to enhancement so everyone has the actual means to exercise freedom, and anarcho-transhumanists define freedom as expanding one's ability to act.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Bostrom lists diversity of races as a value and warns against eugenics; racial hierarchy is contrary to the movement's universalism.

total-state.rationale: Bostrom states that moral objections are not grounds for coercion and that centrally planned efforts to improve people have a poor record, which excludes a state directing all areas of life.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is a transhumanist aim, but territorial expansion between nations is not and conflicts with peace and cooperation.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The movement is committed to democracy and the rule of law, not feudal loyalty.

bound-labor.rationale: Unfree labour contradicts the movement's autonomy and rights commitments.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Transhumanists emphasise reason, research and open discussion as ways to reliable knowledge, though they admit epistemic tentativeness.

universal-morality.rationale: Bostrom speaks of broadly shared values yet stresses pluralism and tentativeness; adherents are split between utilitarian and subjectivist views.

single-common-good.rationale: Bostrom's values stress pluralism in what people consider improvement, so a single common good worked out by reason is not the line.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is unrelated to the movement's programme; the sources never raise it.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Left transhumanists might favour it but other strands do not discuss it.

economic-freedom.rationale: Libertarian transhumanists say so but democratic and left strands disagree.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Transhumanism is rooted in Enlightenment reason and science, though some religious transhumanists exist and the term 'only guide' is strong.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Declaration point 6 asks for global solidarity, which cuts against reserving benefits for citizens.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The democratic strand favours basic income and post-work trends, which oppose work requirements.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Declaration point 3 warns that not all change is progress; sacrificing cultural institutions is not a movement stance.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Transhumanists favour individual morphological freedom and reject appeals to nature, so law prescribing gender roles is opposed.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Bostrom's values list diversity of races and the Declaration calls for inclusive moral vision and equal respect, so racial classification and segregation by law is incompatible.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Left transhumanists might agree; others do not.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no place in the movement, whose values stress open discussion and evidence.

national-mission.rationale: The movement is global in outlook rather than missionary for a national government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Left and democratic strands may agree but the movement has no stance.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Libertarian transhumanists favour a minimal state, while democratic transhumanists want regulation, public research funding and welfare; the movement is split.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Bostrom lists diversity of races as a value, and racial separation conflicts with the Declaration's inclusive moral vision.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Declaration point 6 asks for inclusive moral vision, and point 7 extends well-being to all sentient beings, which includes equal worth of all humans though it goes further.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Declaration point 8 emphasises freedom of personal choice, and the movement opposes coercion over personal beliefs.

population-transfer.rationale: Coercive transfers contradict the movement's rights commitments and Bostrom's stance against coercion.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Libertarian transhumanism rests on a non-aggression-style self-ownership principle, but democratic transhumanists accept state coercion through taxes and regulation; the movement is split.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Libertarian and Extropian strands see competition as an engine, while democratic and left strands stress cooperation.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Left and democratic strands lean yes but libertarians do not.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law is not covered by the sources, and libertarian and democratic strands would differ.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Bostrom lists diversity as a value and the movement is cosmopolitan.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Declaration point 6 requires policy that respects autonomy and individual rights, which conflicts with suspending protections.

party-controls-media.rationale: Declaration point 4 asks for forums for open discussion, which state control of media negates.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of the army conflicts with democratic and rule-of-law commitments.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Bostrom calls for international cooperation and expanded democracy beyond national levels to manage global risks.

clerical-rule.rationale: Religious critics oppose transhumanism and the movement is secular and rights-based.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is a Marxist-Leninist idea absent from the sources.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The movement's emphasis on autonomy and open discussion opposes moral censorship.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not covered; Bostrom favours cooperation but takes no line on alliances.

people-in-arms.rationale: Militia policy is not covered; libertarian and democratic strands would differ.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The movement is techno-urban in orientation, though Viridian design and technogaianism add nuance.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Pluralism is valued, but the movement's progress framing treats some conditions as better than others; split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The movement is science-based and critics note its conflict with religious claims; creationism has no support.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Global solidarity leans yes, but the movement never took up debt.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Declaration point 6 calls for solidarity across the globe and Bostrom argues benefits should reach as many people as possible.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Democratic and left strands accept limits on property for the common good, while libertarians hold self-ownership and property as foundational; split.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Transhumanists criticise precaution as holding back progress, though Declaration point 3 urges care about risks and Bostrom notes epistemic tentativeness; the movement leans against a strong precautionary principle.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Transhumanism is secular and rationalist, so a divine ruler is rejected.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Libertarian members favour it and democratic ones favour progressive taxation; split.

character-from-environment.rationale: Transhumanists emphasise that biology can be altered, while also valuing education; the movement does not choose between nature and nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Bostrom argues for rule of law and democracy.

space-expansion.rationale: Declaration point 1 names confinement to Earth as a limit to overcome, and space is a stated transhumanist goal and part of anarcho-transhumanist demands.

leader-cult.rationale: Personality cults conflict with democratic values and rationalism.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Ethnic territorial claims contradict the movement's universalism and cooperative orientation.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Declaration point 8 asks for wide freedom over personal choices, and the movement stands against coercion on belief.

women-must-cover.rationale: Personal freedom over one's body is central, so compelled dress is opposed.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: A Jewish-politics question the sources do not touch.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Left transhumanists use materialist analysis, while the movement's core holds that technology and ideas drive change; split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The movement is global and open and values international cooperation.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The movement works through democratic institutions and research.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Bostrom rejects imposing a single standard of improvement and the movement favours autonomy.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Left transhumanists predict dystopia from unchecked accumulation, while others are optimistic.

delink-world-market.rationale: The movement stresses global access and integration.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian transhumanists defend freedom of association while democratic ones do not; split.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Declaration point 7 explicitly extends well-being to all sentient beings including animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Point 7 extends well-being to animals, yet transhumanists accept animal research for medical progress; abolitionists such as Pearce want to end all suffering, so adherents are split.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim absent from the sources.

native-born-offices.rationale: The movement's inclusive moral vision is against such restrictions.

party-own-road.rationale: An internal communist debate absent from the sources.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Democratic and rule-of-law commitments reject military guardianship.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Libertarians favour, democratic strands do not; split.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Bostrom's commitment to peace, cooperation, democracy and rule of law, and the Declaration's emphasis on rights, oppose a great power invading an allied country to keep it in a bloc.

democratic-peace.rationale: Bostrom's call to expand democracy for global security aligns with this idea.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A conspiracy view at odds with the movement's reason and open-discussion values.

informal-organisation.rationale: Declaration point 4 calls for a social order capable of responsible decisions; anarcho-transhumanists dissent.

religious-nation.rationale: A secular movement and a religious nation conflict.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The democratic wing wants publicly funded universal health care, and the market-friendly wing favours private provision; the mixed model is compatible with both.

religion-illusion.rationale: Many transhumanists are secular, but religious transhumanists exist, so adherents are split.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Libertarian members say yes, left members dispute it; split.

majority-settlement.rationale: Ethnic settlement policy contradicts universalist and rights values.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Hughes's synthesis of social democracy and liberalism may fit a third way, but libertarian members reject it.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The movement values reason and evidence; denial has no place.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Bostrom's list of values includes diversity of sexual orientations and lifestyles, and Declaration point 8 asks for wide personal freedom, so criminalisation is rejected.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Declaration point 4 calls for forums for open discussion and a social order for responsible decisions; suppression contradicts that.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: A secular, autonomy-based movement opposes blasphemy law.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Contradicts global solidarity and inclusive moral vision.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Secular and autonomy-based, rejects religious test of rulers.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Hughes's radical democracy and techno-progressive calls for accountable authorities support broader participation, though not specifically in workplaces.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Strong technoprogressive views support the right to modify one's body on one's own terms, which includes recognition of gender identity.

assisted-dying.rationale: Declaration point 8 asks for wide freedom over how to end or extend life, though life extension is the focus, so support follows from autonomy.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Twyman describes transhumanism as a hub across politics, and Bostrom's values transcend partisan lines; many adherents argue left-right is outdated, though the strands still sort along it.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Bostrom's values list diversity of creeds, so cultural incompatibility is rejected.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Transhumanism is secular and grounds authority in reason and rights, so I mark a clear no.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Secular leaning but liberty values conflict; split.

social-market-economy.rationale: The democratic wing resembles this, but libertarian members prefer laissez-faire and left members prefer more; no unified line.

rich-first.rationale: Bostrom accepts that early adopters may enjoy benefits first, arguing for speed so benefits reach as many as possible; Hughes seeks to equalise access later.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Democratic and equal-worth commitments reject hereditary rule.

property-franchise.rationale: Bostrom's democracy expansion and equal worth reject it.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Left transhumanists may agree; others not.

racial-franchise.rationale: Bostrom's values list diversity of races and Declaration point 6 calls for inclusive moral vision; racial limits on voting contradict both.

online-participation.rationale: Bostrom backs collaborative information filtering and open discussion, and technoprogressives embrace technology for democracy; adherents see the internet as a participation tool.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Bigoted boycotts contradict the movement's diversity values.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Left and democratic strands warn that capitalist accumulation creates elite access to enhancement, while libertarians reject the premise.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Bostrom's values include diversity of sexual orientation; the liberal movement supports equal service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Autonomy and freedom of belief; the movement is secular but does not coerce.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Only the anarcho strand might support it.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Libertarian members favour charity, democratic members favour state provision; split.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Declaration point 5 names reducing existential risks as an urgent, well-funded priority and Bostrom calls global security the most fundamental requirement.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Transhumanism centres individual autonomy and morphological freedom, which is at odds with state-drilled youth organisations.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Adherents are split by wider politics and the sources are silent on foreign bases.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Democratic transhumanists often back a basic income while libertarians reject redistribution; the strands split.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The movement is secular-humanist and rationalist, treating politics as a matter of reasoned policy toward human flourishing.

god-not-male.rationale: Secular movement indifferent to religious language; some religious transhumanists differ.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Secular movement with no stance on judging religious texts; its humanism is compatible with the idea but does not state it.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Declaration extends concern to all sentient beings and the movement is cosmopolitan, so ethnic economic preference is rejected.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Bostrom's morphological freedom and the Declaration's emphasis on enhancement favour giving patients access sooner, though democratic strands keep safety regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The Declaration treats overcoming ageing as a central aim and technoprogressives propose public funding.

person-over-state.rationale: Bostrom's values and the Declaration put individual choice over one's own life and body first and distrust coercive improvement.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Declaration and Bostrom's values are cosmopolitan and pluralist, concerned for all sentience, so racial political organising does not fit.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Focus is on existential risk and global security, not on when force may be used.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Libertarian strands favour pricing externalities while technoprogressives favour regulation and investment; the sources do not settle it.

future-generations.rationale: The Transhumanist Declaration urges careful deliberation about risks to the long-term future and sustained survival of life, which supports a duty to later generations.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Libertarian strands favour private arms and democratic strands favour state monopoly, so the family is split.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Libertarian strands favour individual contracts and democratic strands favour unions, so the family is split.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Technoprogressives favour income support while libertarians oppose it, so adherents are split.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Libertarian strands back fiscal limits while technoprogressives back flexible state investment.

sacred-nation.rationale: The movement is cosmopolitan and secular, concerned with all sentient beings rather than a sacred nation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The Declaration holds that humanity's current nature is open to redesign through technology.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not an issue the sources discuss, and strands differ on religion.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Left and anarcho strands favour common ownership while libertarian and Extropian strands favour property; the family is split.

self-ownership.rationale: Morphological freedom, the right to choose how to modify one's own body and mind, is central in the Declaration and Bostrom's values.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Democratic transhumanists favour universal health care while libertarians favour minimal targeted help; the family is split.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Libertarian transhumanists accept process-based justice but the democratic mainstream favours fair distribution of technology, so the family is split and leans against.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Technoprogressive transhumanists back automation with shared gains such as basic income, and the libertarian wing welcomes automation too.

missingStatements.text: Individuals should have the legal right to modify their own bodies and minds with technology, including to extend their lives.
missingStatements.rationale: Declaration point 8 and Bostrom's morphological freedom make this the movement's defining claim, going beyond the existing enhancement statement to a legal right including life extension.

missingStatements.text: Reducing the risk of human extinction should be a top priority of public policy.
missingStatements.rationale: Declaration point 5 names reducing existential risks as an urgent, well-funded priority and Bostrom calls global security the most fundamental requirement.

missingStatements.text: Radical life extension and the defeat of aging should be a major goal of publicly funded medical research.
missingStatements.rationale: The Declaration lists overcoming aging as a central aim and democratic transhumanists propose public funding of anti-aging research.

missingStatements.text: Artificial minds and other non-human intelligences, if sentient, deserve moral consideration equal to humans.
missingStatements.rationale: Declaration point 7 extends well-being to all sentient beings including future artificial intelligences and modified humans.

notes: Strands diverge: libertarian transhumanists reject publicly insured enhancement, taxation and regulation, while democratic technoprogressives (Hughes) favour regulation, basic income and universal access, and anarcho- and left strands go further. Economic answers are therefore mostly 0 or low.
